title: Ulysses at Ismarus

scope.description: Ulysses raids Ismarus, delays, and escapes after the Ciconians attack.
scope.boundaryRationale: The Ismarus raid resolves with escape to the ships before the later Lotus-Eater unit.

sourceBoundaryDecision: The Ismarus raid resolves with escape to the ships before the later Lotus-Eater unit.

evidence.sourceText: After leaving Troy in ruins, Ulysses embarked with his men and spoils, and, favored by a good wind, soon came within sight of Ismarus, the home of the worthy and wealthy Ciconians.
After leaving Troy in ruins, Ulysses embarked with his men and spoils, and, favored by a good wind, soon came within sight of Ismarus, the home of the worthy and wealthy Ciconians.
While they were thus employed and entirely off their guard, the neighbors and allies of the Ciconians came upon them unawares, and put many to death.

mainCharacters.reason: Ulysses proposes the raid and escapes with his men.

narrative.synopsis: Ulysses raids Ismarus after leaving Troy, but his men delay until Ciconian allies attack, forcing the Greeks to escape.
narrative.openingSituation: Ulysses reaches Ismarus after leaving Troy.
narrative.centralConflict: His men delay instead of departing after the raid.
storyline: The Greeks embarked and left the Ciconian shores.

evidenceSummary.sourceText: To increase the riches he was carrying home, he proposed to his army to land and storm the city,--a proposal which was enthusiastically received and immediately carried out.

supports.rationale: The exact source sentence directly supports Ulysses proposed attacking Ismarus..
